title: Sign-in
description: How sign-in attempts end, which a credential-stuffing attack changes, and how the checks of the codes that prove an account's email address, the confirmations of password resets, the confirmations of changes of an account's address, and the checks of second factors end, which guessing changes (the auth spec).

panels.title: How do sign-in attempts end?
panels.description: Sign-in attempts in the last 5 minutes, by how each ended: succeeded, challenged, for an account whose second factor then completes it, invalid_credentials, or rate_limited by a sign-in limit (AUTH-004 to AUTH-006, AUTH-058). A rise in invalid_credentials across many emails is the shape of credential stuffing.

panels.title: How do checks of email codes end?
panels.description: Checks of the codes that prove an account's email address in the last 5 minutes, by how each ended: verified, wrong_code, code_expired, or rate_limited by the limit on each user's checks (AUTH-031 to AUTH-033). A rise in wrong_code and rate_limited is the shape of guessing an address's code.

panels.title: How do confirmations of password resets end?
panels.description: Confirmations of password resets in the last 5 minutes, by how each ended: reset, invalid_reset_code, or rate_limited by the limit on an email's confirmations from one client address (AUTH-037 to AUTH-039). A rise in invalid_reset_code across many client addresses is the shape of guessing reset codes, which their 80 bits leave hopeless, and which costs a hash each.

panels.title: How do confirmations of changes of the address end?
panels.description: Confirmations of changes of an account's email address in the last 5 minutes, by how each ended: changed, wrong_code, code_expired, email_in_use, or rate_limited by the limit on each user's checks of codes (AUTH-051, AUTH-052, AUTH-033). A rise in wrong_code across many accounts is the shape of guessing the codes of an address that they each asked for, which the codes' 80 bits leave hopeless.

panels.title: How do checks of second factors end?
panels.description: Checks of second factors' codes in the last 5 minutes, an authenticator app's or a recovery code, at a sign-in's completion, a setup's confirmation, a re-authentication or a change of the password, by how each ended: passed, wrong_code, or rate_limited by the buckets of each user's and each device token's checks (AUTH-056 to AUTH-065). A rise in wrong_code across many accounts is the shape of guessing with stolen passwords, which the buckets bound to 10 guesses a day.

panels.title: How do exchanges of providers' codes end?
panels.description: Exchanges of an OAuth provider's code for the user's identity in the last 5 minutes, by provider and by how each ended: succeeded, rejected, when the provider refused the code, its verifier or its redirect URI, or unavailable, when it failed, refused the API's own client, answered what the API can't read, or didn't answer in time (AUTH-077). A run of unavailable alone is the provider's outage, or a client secret that the deployment set wrong, which SignInProviderUnavailable reports.
